record.paper_title: Some Open Questions in Quiver Gauge Theory
record.context_brief: Generalizing zig-zag paths and perfect matchings
record.original_question: For brane tilings on the torus T^2, zig-zag paths and perfect matchings are central constructions. What are their mathematical and physical roles for general m in the setting of m-graded quivers and generalized brane tilings on T^{m+1}?

evidence.quote: Question 20. For brane tilings on T2, zig-zag paths and perfect matchings are important concepts. Can we reveal their further mathematical and physical implications for general m?

artifact.self_contained_problem:
Background. A brane tiling on the two-torus $T^2$ is a bipartite graph embedded in $T^2$ whose faces, edges, and nodes encode the data of a quiver with superpotential associated to a toric Calabi–Yau threefold. Two combinatorial structures play a fundamental role:

(i) Perfect matchings: collections of edges of the bipartite graph such that every node is incident to exactly one chosen edge. Perfect matchings are in correspondence with points of the toric diagram of the underlying Calabi–Yau threefold and parametrize chiral fields entering the master space and the mesonic moduli space.

(ii) Zig-zag paths: oriented closed paths on the bipartite graph that alternately turn maximally right at one color of node and maximally left at the other. Their homology classes in $H_1(T^2,\mathbb Z)$ reproduce the external legs of the $(p,q)$-web dual to the toric diagram, and they control consistency of the tiling.

These notions admit generalizations to $m$-graded quivers with superpotential, which describe the open-string sector of the topological B-model on Calabi–Yau $(m+2)$-folds. In the toric case, such $m$-graded quivers are encoded by generalized brane tilings ("$m$-dimers") realized as cell complexes on the torus $T^{m+1}$, where the case $m=1$ recovers ordinary brane tilings on $T^2$. Generalized perfect matchings and a Kasteleyn-type construction have been formulated for arbitrary $m$.

Problem. For generalized brane tilings on $T^{m+1}$ associated to $m$-graded quivers with superpotential (with $m \geq 1$):

(a) Formulate, in full generality, intrinsic combinatorial/topological definitions of "zig-zag paths" and "perfect matchings" extending the $m=1$ notions, and identify the homological/cohomological invariants on $T^{m+1}$ that they realize.

(b) Determine the mathematical role of these objects: their relation to the toric diagram of the underlying Calabi–Yau $(m+2)$-fold (e.g. as parametrizations of lattice points or of higher-dimensional faces), to the consistency conditions of the generalized tiling, and to mutation classes of $m$-graded quivers.

(c) Determine their physical role in the corresponding $B$-model / gauge-theoretic setting, including their interpretation in terms of moduli spaces, BPS-like states, and any analog of the $(p,q)$-web for higher $m$.

Provide either a complete theory establishing (a)–(c), or precise structural results that determine these roles for all $m \geq 1$.
artifact.category_tag: Graded quivers and generalized brane tilings
artifact.status_search_result: Generalized perfect matchings for $m$-graded quivers / $m$-dimers have been defined and a Kasteleyn-type algorithm extending the $m=1$ case has been given (Franco–Seong and collaborators, JHEP 11 (2019) 104 and follow-ups), establishing their role in encoding toric data of CY $(m+2)$-folds. A general intrinsic theory of zig-zag paths for arbitrary $m$ on $T^{m+1}$, together with a complete account of their mathematical and physical implications, is not fully developed in the literature found; the question is therefore partially addressed but remains open in its full generality.

status_evidence.title: Graded quivers, generalized dimer models and toric geometry
status_evidence.snippet: M-dimers fully encode the m-graded quivers and their superpotentials in the toric case; perfect matchings are generalized to arbitrary m with a Kasteleyn-matrix-type algorithm.
status_evidence.claim: Perfect matchings have been generalized to arbitrary m with an extension of the Kasteleyn approach.

status_evidence.title: Graded Quivers, Generalized Dimer Models and Toric Geometry (CUNY)
status_evidence.snippet: Generalization of perfect matchings to arbitrary m, with simplified algorithm.
status_evidence.claim: Partial progress on extending perfect matchings to m-graded setting is documented.

status_evidence.title: Twin Theories, Polytope Mutations and Quivers for GTPs
status_evidence.snippet: Discussion of zig-zag paths and brane tilings in the context of generalized toric polygons and quiver theories.
status_evidence.claim: Zig-zag paths continue to be studied in generalized tiling contexts but a complete higher-m theory is not established.
